description: Per-family rung-4 (bounded transformer residency) applicability, derived from the pinned inference revision's provider/architecture code. Read by scripts/generate-memory-matrix.mjs, which turns each (family, backend) verdict into the matrix's bounded_transformer_residency cells. Keys are the family group ids from generate-memory-matrix.mjs#familyGroup, which are the family's MLX story id.

structuralApplicability.full: The windowable transformer trunk is ONE uniform stack of interchangeable blocks; a single BlockPlan bounds essentially all of its weight bytes. Only embedders and heads sit outside it.
structuralApplicability.partial: The trunk is not one uniform stack. Any of: it decomposes into two or more separately-indexed stacks (needing a plan each); its single stack mixes block KINDS, so the residency floor is the largest kind rather than an average block; or part of it — a conv trunk, a second resident network — cannot be windowed at all. `blockStacks` names every stack and marks which are windowable. Neither Implemented nor Structurally N/A — recorded as partial rather than rounded to either (SC-15969).
structuralApplicability.none: No uniform sequential block stack exists, so the rung has nothing to bound. Requires `structural` evidence; the matrix cell becomes Structurally N/A.
structuralApplicability.requires-different-primitive: A uniform stack exists, but gen_core::block_window's SHAPE (one carried state, a fresh view per window, release after materialize) cannot express this family's forward. Recorded as a finding rather than as an N/A, per the story: a family that needs a different PRIMITIVE is not a family the rung cannot help. Such a family may never be marked implemented.

implementation.provider-local: Real block streaming that does NOT go through the shared primitive.
implementation.none: No block-window code path exists for this family on this backend.

vocabulary.implementedEntries: The exact catalog entries whose provider exposes the rung-4 code path. Implementation is per ENTRY, not per family — Krea's Candle contract is gated on the turbo descriptor id, so krea_2_raw does not get it — and a family-level claim would over-report. Must be empty exactly when `implementation` is "none".
vocabulary.implementedModes: Optional narrowing of `implementedEntries` to the catalog modes the implementing provider descriptor actually serves. Needed because the matrix collapses a catalog entry's modes onto one provider id while inference may route them to DIFFERENT descriptors: Candle Krea's edit modes are served by the krea_2_edit descriptor and the krea_2_turbo_edit surface tag, neither of which returns the memory contract, so a mode-blind claim would report rung 4 as implemented on a route that does not expose it. Absent means every mode.
vocabulary.implementedTiers: Optional narrowing of `implementedEntries` to measured numeric tiers. Absent means every tier. Lens uses this because dense BF16 moves the request peak while Q4 does not; treating a family-level implementation as tier-neutral would turn a measured non-win into a production claim.
vocabulary.implementedOverlays: Optional narrowing of `implementedEntries` to the overlay cells admitted by the provider contract. Absent means every overlay. Use this for evidence-gated exclusions such as a contract measured only with no adapter; use `overlayIncompatible` instead when the provider mechanism makes an overlay structurally impossible.
vocabulary.strategyParameters: The rung's OWN published parameters for an implemented family. Deliberately not the cumulative composition: rung 4 engages rungs 2 and 3 by cost-order default, but this survey has no measured tile/chunk values for the families it marks implemented, and inventing them would put unmeasured numbers in a cell that reads as evidence.
vocabulary.overlayIncompatible: Present when the provider's adapter mechanism makes a windowed block unable to carry an overlay. It makes the overlay cells of the IMPLEMENTED entries/modes Structurally N/A with the cited evidence, and nothing else: on an entry that has no streaming path at all the rung is Missing for the ordinary reason, and calling it structurally exempt would presuppose a path that does not exist. It is reported on the cell as its own `overlayIncompatible` flag rather than by overwriting `structuralApplicability`, whose meaning is about the ARCHITECTURE — Krea's 28-block trunk is windowable whatever its adapters do.
vocabulary.blockStacks[].entries: Optional. Present when a stack exists on only some of the family's catalog entries, so a per-entry difference stays machine-readable instead of being rounded into the family verdict.

requestPeak.moves: Measured to move the REQUEST peak, not merely a phase peak.
requestPeak.does-not-move: Measured, and the request peak did not move. Per the epic's non-negotiable this is not a saving and must not be selected by default.
requestPeak.unmeasured: No request-peak measurement exists for this family/backend at the pinned revision.

vocabulary.requestPeak.byTier: Optional per-tier override of the family/backend request-peak finding. Required when measurements differ by numeric tier; omitted tiers inherit requestPeak.finding.
vocabulary.requestPeak.scopes: Optional exact cell selectors for measurements narrower than a whole family/backend or tier. Each selector may name entries, tiers, modes, and overlays; omitted dimensions are wildcards. A matching selector overrides byTier and finding.

notes: Rung 4 requires rung 1 engaged in the same request (gen_core::memory_strategy BOUNDED_TRANSFORMER_RESIDENCY_REQUIRES). That prerequisite is NOT restated per family here: the generator reads it from the same rung-1 predicate it already uses for the staged_residency cells, so a family that gains rung-1 capability stops reporting the prerequisite gap without a survey edit.

Structural applicability is about the DENOISE trunk. The component-scope axis (Dit / TextEncoder / Both) is a published rung-4 parameter, not a separate rung; where a family's text encoder changes the answer it is recorded in `findings`.

Overlay compatibility is a property of the provider's ADAPTER MECHANISM, not of the architecture: a provider that installs adapters as forward-time residuals can replay them onto a materialized block, while one that folds a delta into the base weight at load cannot. Only the two families with code evidence either way carry an `overlays` finding.

Why `unmeasured` is the honest answer almost everywhere, and why a static proxy will not do. docs/sc-16195/resolution-sweep.json measures, at 1024x1024 on the RESIDENT hold-all path, weight residency against activation transient: illustrious q8 4.74 vs 14.04 GiB, sdxl bf16 6.48 vs 14.04, z-image-turbo q4 5.38 vs 14.04, lens q4 16.46 vs 14.04, qwen-image q8 33.45 vs 7.66, krea-2-turbo q8 18.06 vs 7.67. Weight residency is a MINORITY of that peak on three of the six tiers, which is enough to show rung 4 cannot be assumed to move the request peak — but not enough to predict that it will not, because rung 4 is only ever selected in composition with rungs 2 and 3, which attack exactly the transient term those rows are dominated by. Z-Image is the worked case: its resident-path row looks transient-bound, and once the ladder is engaged its request peak is decode-bound at ~4.36 GiB and rung 4 still moved it. So this axis is decided by a per-family measurement of the rung-3 composition against the rung-4 composition, which is what Krea's Candle evidence records and what no other family has.

What `blockStacks` covers, stated once. It inventories the stacks resident during the DENOISE phase — the trunk a rung-4 window would bound, plus any second network held alongside it (a control branch, an identity path, a second expert), because those set the share of resident transformer weight the rung can actually move. It does NOT inventory text-encoder or vision-tower stacks: those belong to the conditioning phase, they are what rung 1 sheds, and the component-scope parameter (Dit / TextEncoder / Both) is the axis that addresses them. Where a family's encoder changes the rung-4 answer it is recorded in `findings` instead.

mlx.summary: One uniform 12-block dual-stream stack. Windowable in principle; the smallest N in the catalog, so the ceiling on the saving is the lowest.

evidence.reason: MageTransformer holds a single `blocks: Vec<MageTransformerBlock>` built over `0..cfg.depth` from one constructor — a uniform sequential stack, each block consuming the previous pair.
`depth: 12` with `depth_single_blocks = 0` — every block is dual-stream, so the trunk is one homogeneous run rather than a double/single split.
The provider contract declares Resident Implemented and every other rung Missing, so no rung-4 code path exists.

requestPeak.reason: No rung-4 run exists for Mage-Flow on either backend.

findings: N = 12 is the smallest uniform stack surveyed. A window of 1 bounds trunk weights at 1/12, against ~1/30 on z-image and ~1/60 on Qwen-Image — applicable, but the least leverage per unit of re-materialization cost.

Mage-Flow is TE-heavy: the conditioning encoder is a full decoder stack of its own (text_encoder/layer.rs). A Dit-scoped window bounds only the 12-block trunk, so the component scope, not the window size, is the parameter that decides whether rung 4 is worth anything here.

candle.summary: Same uniform 12-block dual-stream trunk as the MLX twin. The shared Candle block-window backend exists, but Mage exposes neither a memory-strategy contract nor a family loader that can drive it.

evidence.reason: The Candle port carries the same 12-block dual-stream trunk and declares no memory_strategy_contract, so it exposes no rung-4 capability.
Candle implements the shared BlockWindowBackend adapter, but the Mage provider has no streamed-block loader wired to candle_gen::block_window::run_windowed, so this family cannot drive it.

requestPeak.reason: No rung-4 run exists for Mage-Flow on either backend.

mlx.summary: The shipped rung-4 exemplar, and still partial: the base DiT is three stacks (2 noise refiners, 2 context refiners, 30 unified layers) and only the 30-layer stack is windowed. The control route adds two more — a 15-block control stack, which IS windowed, and a 2-block control refiner, which is not. The refiner blocks stay resident either way.

evidence.reason: The transformer holds `noise_refiner: Vec<ZImageTransformerBlock>`, `context_refiner: Vec<ZImageContextBlock>` and `layers: Vec<ZImageTransformerBlock>`; the rung-4 arming path records only the `layers` prefix as re-readable, so the two refiner stacks are outside the window.

The control route adds `control_layers: Vec<ZImageControlBlock>` (15 blocks at base places 0,2,...,28) and arms rung 4 for it with the `control_layers` prefix, so the streamer covers the control stack as well as the base trunk.
Family-side half of rung 4: rebuilds block n from the snapshot per window and drains the view with `remove_accessed`, driving mlx_gen::block_residency::run_windowed.

Declares BoundedTransformerResidency Implemented only when the load is a re-openable `WeightsSource::Dir` with `LoadShape::DeferredMaterialization`, and publishes transformer_window_sizes = [1] plus all three component scopes.

requestPeak.reason: Measured on real weights: the staged denoise peak falls 4.653 -> 1.795 GiB (q4), 7.486 -> 2.149 (q8) and 13.362 -> 3.201 (bf16), which moves the request peak off the denoise phase entirely — after rung 4 all three tiers are decode-bound at ~4.36 GiB.

evidence.reason: Real-weight residency suite that exercises the windowed forward against the fully-resident control.
Module docs carry the measured window ladder (window 1 = 8.0 MiB vs 238.4 MiB resident, linear in window size) and the materialize-guard control.

findings: The window size is INERT above 1 on this family: 30/15/8/4/2 all land on the same peak and an all-covering attribution control matches window 8 exactly, so `TRANSFORMER_WINDOW_SIZES` publishes [1] rather than a ladder.

Component scope and streamability are two different levers and must not be conflated. Making the encoder streamable at all under Sequential is what let bf16 fit 8 GB (conditioning 8.489 -> 2.718 GiB); the tunable TextEncoder scope cuts conditioning a further 46.5% and moves the request peak 0.0%, which is why the published default is Dit — see gen-core's memory_strategy prerequisite note.

Overlays are compatible here, in contrast to Krea/Candle: adapters are installed as forward-time residuals and `BlockAdapters` replays the captured list onto each materialized block, so a LoRA-carrying request can still stream.

The declaration is per LOAD, and the matrix has no load-source axis. Rung 4 is Missing for a single-file / ComfyUI load, because streaming rebuilds blocks from the snapshot per window and an in-memory `Weights` has no re-openable source. Every catalog route here is a `WeightsSource::Dir` registry load, so the cells are right for the routes the matrix covers — but a consumer must not read them as covering a user-imported single-file checkpoint.

Packed-tier LoRA residual plans are retained and replayed onto every materialized main block, so none, LoRA, and strict-control overlays all expose the same request-scoped rung.

evidence.reason: The CUDA provider contracts publish the full ladder, exact bounded-host-decode/chunk/window candidate ranges, one shared calibration identity, explicit PiD refusal, and overlay-compatible rung-4 support for both registered and bespoke control routes.

The streamed packed DiT retains its host-backed transformer view, materializes one whole main-layer window, and drives candle_gen::block_window::run_windowed with synchronized release and ragged-final-window coverage.
The ignored CUDA real-weight conformance covers packed q4/q8 base and Fun-Controlnet loading plus fixed-seed warm repeat, request-field steering, recoverable errors, and cancellation cleanup.

The fresh-process CUDA harness selects every rung, installed q4/q8/bf16 tier, optional deterministic LoRA overlay, and text-to-image or reference-driven style-variation mode while recording phase peaks and warm-repeat determinism.
The strict-control CUDA harness drives the shipping Fun-Controlnet Union 2.1 checkpoint through every rung and installed tier, recording predecode/decode peaks and fixed-seed output.

requestPeak.reason: Fresh-process CUDA calibration on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell at 1024² moves the strict-control request envelope from resident 27.117/32.016/40.573 GB (q4/q8/bf16) to approximately 13.6/13.7/13.3 GB with one-block streaming; the denoise phase becomes bounded by a single materialized main/control block window.

mlx.summary: The shared block-window primitive rebuilds the uniform 60-block base/edit DiT one block at a time for BF16, packed Q4/Q8, and captured LoRA/LoKr residuals. The optional five-block control side branch is structurally windowable but is not implemented by this MLX provider path, so the distinct qwen_image_control provider does not advertise rung 3 or 4.

evidence.reason: QwenTransformer holds a single `blocks: Vec<QwenTransformerBlock>` over `0..cfg.num_layers` (60); everything else is embedders and the output head.

The Fun-Controlnet-Union route adds `QwenFunControlBranch { blocks: Vec<QwenTransformerBlock> }` — 5 FULL dual-stream blocks at `control_layers = [0, 12, 24, 36, 48]` — held in the heavy bundle alongside the 60-block base trunk for the whole denoise.
QwenBlockStream reopens the production checkpoint, rebuilds one mapped block per shared window, drains its source aliases, and replays packed quantization plus captured adapter residuals.
The load-exact contract publishes DiT window 1 only for sequential deferred directory loads and explicitly leaves bounded attention and transformer residency Missing on qwen_image_control.

requestPeak.reason: Authoritative base/no-overlay ladder runs measured bounded attention versus bounded transformer residency at 64,574,244,508 versus 16,128,899,280 allocator bytes for BF16, 33,921,472,156 versus 15,977,855,160 for Q4, and 44,091,560,604 versus 15,977,855,160 for Q8. SC-16353's separate unbounded-window-60-versus-window-1 same-stream attribution did not move the conditioning-dominated request peak; that control is retained as an attribution result rather than substituted for the rung-3-versus-rung-4 ladder measurements.

evidence.reason: Authoritative base BF16/Q4/Q8 no-overlay provider records compare complete bounded-attention and bounded-transformer-residency requests on pinned artifacts, fixtures, inference revisions, and calibration fingerprints.

findings: The five-block QwenFunControlBranch is structurally windowable because it is the same uniform QwenTransformerBlock stack, but the MLX control provider does not implement its block stream in this change. It is a real resident remainder, and qwen_image_control is excluded from rung 3/4 instead of inheriting a family-level claim.

Window 1 is the sole bounded production cadence. The same-stream window-60-versus-window-1 attribution control did not move the conditioning-bound request peak, while the authoritative complete rung-3-versus-rung-4 requests moved the peak by 75.02% for BF16, 52.90% for Q4, and 63.76% for Q8.
The Q4 and Q8 rung-4 captures passed output-equivalence thresholds, range verification, loadability, cleanup, cancellation/error-path scenarios, and the required negative mutation check.

candle.summary: The Candle/CUDA provider reopens the uniform 60-block base/edit DiT from dense mmap tensors or content-addressed packed sidecars and materializes exact shared block windows. The head and tail remain resident. Adapter-bearing requests, including Lightning's built-in LoRA, retain the established additive/folded path and report rung 4 Missing.

evidence.reason: The Candle provider publishes the full base/edit ladder, exact candidate ranges and fingerprint, staged prerequisites, explicit PiD/control/adapter exclusions, and request cleanup behavior.

Dense and packed loaders retain a static source and replay one exact `candle_gen::block_window::BlockPlan` window at a time, with cancellation checks, synchronization before release, and ragged-final-window parity coverage.

requestPeak.reason: SC-15817's representative base-Q4 CUDA capture loaded the exact current artifact and measured the bounded-attention and window-1 transformer compositions at the same 29,700,915,200-byte request peak because conditioning remained dominant. The capture is candidate/gated conformance rather than promotion evidence; unmeasured sibling tiers, modes, and overlays still require their own calibration stories.

evidence.reason: Schema-valid real-weight records bind all five rungs to the exact artifact, CUDA device, load shape, paired repository revisions, phase peaks, and passed loadability without promoting a fit.

findings: Head-once/tail-tiled VAE decode exposes 768, 640, 512, 448, 384, 320, and 256 output-pixel tile edges at overlap 64. Overlap 96 remains only the rejected sub-512 experiment arm.
Lightning and all user-adapter requests preserve their pre-story semantics through the existing additive/folded path and do not inherit the no-overlay rung-4 claim.
The five-block control branch and PiD decoder remain explicit exclusions rather than being inferred from the family-level base implementation.

mlx.summary: The 48-block DiT remains resident, while the TE-dominant 24-layer gpt-oss encoder is rebuilt one layer at a time through the shared block-window driver. The production contract is deliberately narrower than the structural family verdict: dense BF16, Sequential, deferred directory loads, no adapter, and TextEncoder/window=1 only.

evidence.reason: LensTransformer holds a single `blocks: Vec<LensTransformerBlock>` over `0..cfg.num_layers` (48).
The encoder is a uniform stack of GptOssDecoderLayer, so a TextEncoder-scoped window is structurally available too.

LensTextBlockSource rebuilds each exact GptOssDecoderLayer from a re-openable weights view, drains accessed tensors, replays quantization, materializes the carried state, and delegates scheduling to mlx_gen::block_residency::run_windowed.

The provider declares BoundedTransformerResidency Implemented only for BF16 + Sequential + DeferredMaterialization + directory weights with no quantization, adapter, or PiD overlay, publishing TextEncoder/window=1.
Both lens and lens_turbo descriptors expose the measured contract and select the streamable text loader only when the exact production predicate holds; Resident keeps the fully resident encoder.

requestPeak.reason: Real Lens-Turbo BF16 weights on Apple/Metal measured 80.084 GiB unscoped versus 10.037 GiB with TextEncoder/window=1 for the full request, an 87.5% reduction with identical pixels. Q4 is an explicit counterexample: conditioning fell 3.972 -> 1.861 GiB, but the request peak changed 6.367 -> 6.547 GiB, so Q4 remains Missing rather than inheriting the BF16 result.

evidence.reason: Fresh-process, real-weight request comparison pins the BF16 win and the reproducible Q4 non-win while requiring exact generated-pixel identity.
Real-weight window sweep records conditioning peaks by window, exact conditioning identity, prompt-length behavior, and a zero-layer mutation control.

findings: The gpt-oss encoder is MoE. A window over its layers materializes ALL experts of each layer in the window, not the top-k a token routes to, so the per-block cost of a TE-scoped window is the full expert set — a parameter-sizing consequence, not a blocker.

Dense BF16 conditioning scales with the resident window: 80.098 GiB at 24 layers, 33.136 at 8, 21.271 at 4, 15.340 at 2, and 8.767 at 1. Exact identity held at windows 1, 4, and 24; replacing the 24-layer stack with zero layers changed the output by 1.2079592e4, proving the bound is load-bearing.

Lens does not pad every prompt to one fixed token length. Its harmony preamble is fixed, but the measured prompts produced 121, 141, and 181 tokens; window=1 conditioning peaks were 8.748, 8.767, and 8.807 GiB respectively.
The Q4 tier is not a production rung-4 win: its isolated conditioning peak improved, but its full-request peak reproducibly increased. The tier-specific implementation claim is therefore BF16 only.

Adapter cells remain Missing, not Structurally N/A. The provider also rejects PiD for this measured contract, although PiD is a request option rather than an overlay axis in this matrix. The TextEncoder primitive is not inherently incapable of coexisting with either; separate dynamic evidence would be required before broadening the production predicate.

The declaration is per load and the matrix has no load-source or materialization axis. Catalog Lens routes use deferred directory loads, which are re-openable; a single-file, eager, or Resident load does not receive this contract.

A second, independent gpt-oss stack exists: `LensReasonerModel.layers` (24) sits OUTSIDE the Sequential seam, which only knows the text and heavy bundles, so nothing on this ladder sheds it. It is LATENT rather than live: `attach_reasoner` has no production callers and the registry path leaves it off, so no catalog route reaches it today. It matters only if a route ever turns it on.

candle.summary: Same uniform 48-block trunk; no Candle block-window path.

evidence.reason: The Candle Lens provider declares no memory_strategy_contract and does not advertise sequential offload, so neither rung 4 nor its rung-1 prerequisite is reachable.

mlx.summary: One uniform 42-layer decoder stack — but it is BOTH the conditioning encoder and the denoiser, and each layer carries two parallel dense paths of which a forward uses one. The stack shape is fine; the two consequences are findings.

blockStacks.name: layers
blockStacks.blocks: 42 (each holding two parallel dense paths, so ~84 layers' weights)

evidence.reason: Qwen3Backbone holds one `layers: Vec<Layer>` over `0..cfg.llm.num_hidden_layers` (42). Each layer carries two parallel DENSE stacks — an understanding path and a generation path (`_mot_gen` weights) — and a forward runs exactly one of them.

t2i_generate prefills a KV cache on the understanding path, optionally runs an autoregressive think rollout, then denoises by re-running the SAME 42-layer stack on the generation path per step with `update_cache=False`.

requestPeak.reason: No rung-4 run exists for SenseNova.

findings: The `TextEncoder` component scope is structurally N/A for this family: there is no separate text encoder. Conditioning and denoise are the same 42 layers, so the scope axis collapses to a single component and only `Dit` is meaningful.

Per-block bytes are ~2x what a forward reads, because both dense paths live in the same layer. A window that opens the layer wholesale materializes the unused path too; a useful rung-4 here needs a path-filtered view, which is a loader parameter rather than a change to the primitive.

The bound must be phase-scoped. Windowing the denoise forward re-materializes the stack once per step; windowing the prefill/think rollout would re-materialize it once per TOKEN. The plan is per-forward-pass, so a rung-4 selection for this family has to name the denoise phase explicitly rather than the generator.

mlx.summary: Two uniform sub-stacks — 19 double-stream joint blocks then 38 single-stream blocks. One BlockPlan per sub-stack; the residency floor is one double block, which is the larger of the two block kinds.

evidence.reason: FluxTransformer holds `blocks: Vec<JointBlock>` and `single_blocks: Vec<SingleBlock>` built from separate constructors over `num_layers` (19) and `num_single_layers` (38), run as two consecutive loops.
The control route adds `FluxControlNet { blocks: Vec<JointBlock> }` — a partial copy of the base MMDiT, `num_layers: 6` for the shipped Shakker Union-Pro-2.0 — resident alongside the base trunk.

requestPeak.reason: No rung-4 run exists for FLUX.1.

findings: Heterogeneity here does NOT collapse the saving, which is the case the story's warning is aimed at. The two block kinds are internally uniform, so windowing each independently leaves a floor of one double block against a trunk of 19 double + 38 single — a large bound, not a degenerate one. The warning bites when a single outsized block sets the floor, which is not this shape.
